questions.question: What type of storage service is Amazon S3?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is an object storage service.

questions.question: Match each Amazon S3 component with its description.
questions.explanation: Buckets hold objects; keys identify objects; prefixes imply folders.

pairs.right: Regional container for objects
Data referenced by a URL inside a bucket
Value that identifies an object in the bucket
Implies a folder structure

questions.question: S3 buckets are global resources that are not located in any Region.
questions.explanation: Each bucket is Regional and has a Region-specific endpoint.

questions.question: Which bucket name is valid?
questions.explanation: Names: 3–63 chars, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens. No uppercase or underscores.

questions.question: S3 bucket names only need to be unique within your AWS account.
questions.explanation: Bucket names must be globally unique.

questions.question: Which factors should you consider when choosing the Region for a bucket?
questions.explanation: Deciding factors: latency, cost, regulatory requirements.
options: The programming language of your SDK
Bucket name length and key prefix

questions.question: How do you create an implied folder structure in an S3 bucket?
questions.explanation: Prefixes imply a folder structure in an S3 bucket.

questions.question: Match each S3 upload rule with its size.
questions.explanation: Single PUT ≤ 5 GB, multipart recommended >100 MB, required >5 GB, max object 5 TB.

pairs.left: Maximum size for a single PUT
pairs.right: 5 GB
100 MB
5 TB
1 week

questions.question: You must upload a 20 GB file to S3. What must you use?
questions.explanation: Multipart upload is required for objects over 5 GB.

questions.question: If a multipart upload is interrupted, you must restart the whole upload from the beginning.
questions.explanation: Multipart upload can resume where it left off and uploads parts in parallel.

questions.question: You should use multipart upload for objects larger than 100 MB.
questions.explanation: Recommended (should) above 100 MB; required (must) above 5 GB.

questions.question: After versioning has been enabled on a bucket, what can you do?
questions.explanation: Once enabled, versioning can only be suspended, not disabled.
options: Delete it from the bucket settings
Nothing can change it, not even suspension

questions.question: In a versioning-enabled bucket, deleting an object by key only adds a delete marker instead of permanently deleting it.
questions.explanation: The delete marker becomes the current version; GET returns 404.

questions.question: In a versioned bucket, how do you permanently delete an object?
questions.explanation: You must delete each individual version with its version ID.
options: Send DELETE with the key and the version ID of each version
Send DELETE with only the key

questions.question: Versioning helps you recover from unintended user actions and application failures.
questions.explanation: Purpose of versioning.

questions.question: Without versioning, deleting an object by its key deletes it permanently.
questions.explanation: With versioning disabled, DELETE permanently removes the object.

questions.question: Match each S3 server-side encryption option with who manages the keys.
questions.explanation: Three SSE options.

pairs.right: Amazon S3-managed keys
AWS KMS-managed keys
Customer-provided keys

questions.question: How is data in transit to Amazon S3 secured?
questions.explanation: In transit: HTTPS (SSL/TLS) and client-side encryption before transmission.
options: SSL/TLS-encrypted HTTPS endpoints and client-side encryption

questions.question: SSE-C means Amazon S3 generates and manages the encryption keys for you.
questions.explanation: SSE-C uses customer-provided keys. SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys.

questions.question: By default, all Amazon S3 buckets and objects are private.
questions.explanation: Only the AWS account that created the resource can access it by default.

questions.question: Match each S3 access mechanism with its description.
questions.explanation: Access controls for S3.

pairs.right: Attached to IAM users, groups and roles
Resource-based JSON policy with granular permissions
Basic read/write permissions for other AWS accounts
Temporary PUT or GET access to one object
Lets a web app from another domain access bucket resources

questions.question: Whose permissions does a presigned URL use?
questions.explanation: Presigned URLs use the permissions of the creator.
options: The bucket owner root user always
The person who opens the URL
The user who created the URL

questions.question: A presigned URL lets the holder perform any action on the bucket.
questions.explanation: It only allows the PUT or GET it was created for, nothing else.

questions.question: JavaScript on www.example.com must load resources from an S3 bucket in a different domain. What must you configure?
questions.explanation: CORS allows apps loaded in one domain to interact with resources in another.

questions.question: A mobile app must let users upload one photo to a private S3 bucket without giving them AWS credentials. What is the best solution?
questions.explanation: Presigned URLs give temporary PUT/GET on one object using the creator's permissions.
options: Generate a presigned URL for a PUT on that object
Share an IAM user access key in the app

questions.question: A company must be able to recover objects that users delete or overwrite by mistake. What should they enable?
questions.explanation: Versioning keeps previous versions and turns deletes into delete markers.

questions.question: Drag each protection into the right category.
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects data in transit; server-side encryption protects data at rest. Client-side encryption covers both.

questions.question: Drag each S3 access control into its policy type.
questions.explanation: Resource-based policies attach to the bucket/object; identity-based attach to users, groups, roles.

items.item: Policy attached to an IAM user
Policy attached to an IAM role

questions.question: You upload an object named menu.pdf to an S3 bucket named cafe-site in the eu-west-1 Region. Which URL can a client use to access the object?
questions.explanation: Virtual-host-style URL: http://<bucket-name>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<object-key>. The bucket name is part of the domain and the object key comes after the slash.

questions.question: You enable static website hosting on a bucket named cafe-site in eu-west-1. Which URL is the website endpoint?
questions.explanation: Website endpoint structure: http://<bucket-name>.s3-website-<aws-region>.amazonaws.com. Static website hosting must be enabled first.

questions.question: Amazon S3 supports server-side processing, such as PHP or ASP.NET scripts, for websites hosted in a bucket.
questions.explanation: S3 hosts static websites only. Pages can contain client-side scripts, but S3 does not support server-side scripting.

questions.question: A static website hosted on Amazon S3 can include client-side scripts.
questions.explanation: Static pages may contain client-side scripts; only server-side scripting is unsupported.

questions.question: You need to host a static website on Amazon S3. Which of the following are required? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Configure the bucket for website hosting, upload the content, and allow public read access. No servers are needed and server-side scripts are not supported.
options: Launch an EC2 instance as a web server
Upload the website content to the bucket
Enable server-side scripting on the bucket
Give the bucket public read access
Enable static website hosting on the bucket

questions.question: Which of the following are common use cases for Amazon S3? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: S3 use cases: content storage and distribution, backup and restore, archiving, data lakes, big data analytics, disaster recovery and static website hosting.
options: Data lakes and big data analytics

questions.question: Amazon S3 is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) of durability.
questions.explanation: S3 is designed for 11 nines of durability.

questions.question: Match each S3 object metadata item to its type.
questions.explanation: System-defined metadata is set by S3; some of it (storage class, server-side encryption) you can modify. User-defined metadata uses the x-amz-meta- prefix.

pairs.right: System-defined, controlled by S3
System-defined, but you can modify it
System-defined, but you can modify it
User-defined

questions.question: Amazon S3 can respond to event triggers.
questions.explanation: Slide 8 lists 'Can respond to event triggers' as an S3 feature: you can configure event notifications, for example when an object is created, deleted or restored.

questions.question: You configure Amazon S3 event notifications for when objects are created. Which services can receive these notifications? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Per slide 8 notes, S3 event notifications can be used with AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS and Amazon SQS.

questions.question: How many characters can an S3 bucket name have?
questions.explanation: Slide 13: bucket names must be at least 3 and no more than 63 characters long.

questions.question: Which characters are allowed in an S3 bucket name? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 13: use only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; do not use uppercase characters or underscores.

questions.question: After you create an S3 bucket, you can rename it if the new name is globally unique.
questions.explanation: Slide 13 notes: after you create an S3 bucket, you can't change the bucket name, so choose it carefully.

questions.question: You can move an existing S3 bucket to a different Region by changing its Region setting.
questions.explanation: Slide 14 notes: after you create a bucket, you cannot change its Region.

questions.question: Objects stored in an AWS Region never leave that Region unless you explicitly transfer them to another Region.
questions.explanation: Slide 10 notes: each bucket is Regional, and its objects never leave the Region unless you explicitly transfer them.

questions.question: A bucket contains the keys 2021/english/john.txt, 2021/math/john.txt, 2021/math/maria.txt and 2021/summary.txt. You query the bucket with the prefix 2021/math. Which keys are returned?
questions.explanation: Slide 16: a prefix limits results to only those objects whose keys begin with that prefix.

questions.question: The S3 PUT operation lets you update only part of an existing object.
questions.explanation: Slide 20 notes: Amazon S3 always writes the entire object; you cannot do partial updates to an object.

questions.question: Which are benefits of using multipart upload? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 20: multipart upload allows parallel uploading, can resume where it left off, and parts can be uploaded independently in any order. The maximum object size is still 5 TB.
options: Objects larger than 5 TB can be stored
A failed part can be resumed without affecting other parts
Parts can be uploaded independently and in any order
Parts can be uploaded in parallel to improve throughput
Objects are automatically encrypted with SSE-C

questions.question: Your application runs on a low-bandwidth connection and can only process part of a large S3 object at a time. How should it retrieve the data?
questions.explanation: Slide 22: GET can retrieve a range of bytes, which is useful when network connectivity is low or the application can only process subsets of object data.
options: GET the complete object in one request
GET a range of bytes of the object

questions.question: In a versioning-enabled bucket, a user sends DELETE with only the key of photo.gif. Another user then sends a GET for photo.gif without a version ID. What happens?
questions.explanation: Slide 25 notes: deleting with only the key adds a delete marker that becomes the current version, and a request to retrieve that object returns 404 Not Found.
options: S3 returns a 404 Not Found error
S3 returns a 403 Access Denied error
S3 returns the previous version of photo.gif

questions.question: Versioning is enabled by default on new S3 buckets.
questions.explanation: Slide 23 notes: by default, versioning is disabled in S3 buckets.

questions.question: In a versioning-enabled bucket, two objects can have the same key but different version IDs.
questions.explanation: Slide 23: each object has a version ID, so photo.gif can exist as version 111111 and version 121212 in the same bucket.

questions.question: Versioned S3 buckets support object locking.
questions.explanation: Slide 23: versioned buckets support object locking; S3 Object Lock prevents data from being changed, overwritten or deleted.

questions.question: When you enable server-side encryption on a bucket, S3 also encrypts the objects that were already stored in it.
questions.explanation: Slide 28 notes: S3 does not encrypt objects already in the bucket; it only encrypts objects added after encryption is enabled.

questions.question: A company needs server-side encryption for S3 objects and an audit trail of when the encryption key was used and by whom. Which option should it choose?
questions.explanation: Slide 28 notes: SSE-KMS provides an audit trail of when your key was used and by whom, and requires additional permissions for the envelope key.

questions.question: Which data protection option means YOU manage the encryption process, the encryption keys and the related tools before the data reaches S3?
questions.explanation: Slide 28 notes: with client-side encryption you encrypt data on the client side and upload it, managing the process, keys and tools yourself. With SSE-C you provide keys but S3 performs the encryption.

questions.question: Amazon S3 supports both identity-based policies and resource-based policies for managing access.
questions.explanation: Slides 29 and 34: Amazon S3 has two types of access policies, identity-based (attached to IAM users, groups, roles) and resource-based (attached to S3 resources).

questions.question: Which access mechanism is used to grant basic read/write permissions on a bucket or object to other AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: Slide 30: ACLs are resource-based access policies used to grant basic read/write permissions to other AWS accounts, at the bucket or object level.

questions.question: Account B uploads objects into a bucket owned by Account A. What is the only way to manage access to those objects?
questions.explanation: Slide 30 notes: an object ACL is the only way to manage access to objects the bucket owner does not own; the account that created the object grants permissions with object ACLs.
options: An IAM role in Account A
Object ACLs set by Account B
A bucket policy written by Account A
A CORS configuration on the bucket

questions.question: Bucket policies supplement, and in many cases replace, ACL-based access policies.
questions.explanation: Slide 31 notes: bucket policies are resource-based IAM policies that supplement, and in many cases replace, ACL-based access policies.

questions.question: Which must you provide when you create a presigned URL? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 32: you provide security credentials, a bucket name, an object key, an HTTP method and an expiration date and time. The URL uses the creator's permissions.
options: The IAM user name of the person who will use the URL
The bucket name and object key

questions.question: You host a web font in an S3 bucket, and a webpage in a different domain uses that font. The browser blocks the font. What should you configure on the bucket?
questions.explanation: Slide 33 notes: the browser performs a CORS check when a page in another domain loads a web font from your bucket, so CORS must be enabled on the bucket.

questions.question: Match each requirement with the S3 use case it describes.
questions.explanation: Slide 9 notes: data lakes are centralized repositories; DR uses Cross-Region Replication; lifecycle policies archive to S3 Glacier; content can be distributed from S3 or CloudFront.

pairs.left: Store structured and unstructured data at any scale in a central repository for analytics
pairs.right: Data lake

pairs.left: Automatically copy objects to a bucket in another Region to protect critical data
pairs.right: Disaster recovery

pairs.left: Move rarely accessed data to S3 Glacier with lifecycle policies
pairs.right: Backup and archive

pairs.left: Distribute images and videos directly or through CloudFront edge locations
pairs.right: Content storage and distribution

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for:
questions.explanation: AWS: security of the cloud. Customer: security in the cloud.

questions.question: Match the security concept to its question.
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity; authorization uses policies; requesters are principals.

pairs.right: Who is requesting access?
What should they be allowed to do?
A person or application making a request

questions.question: Authentication decides what actions a principal is allowed to perform.
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes who; authorization decides what they can do.

questions.question: Match each IAM entity with its description.
questions.explanation: Users, groups, roles, policies.

pairs.right: Person or application with long-term credentials
Collection of users sharing permissions
Identity that provides temporary credentials when assumed
Document that lists permissions

questions.question: An IAM role has long-term credentials such as a password or access keys.
questions.explanation: Roles have no long-term credentials; assuming a role gives temporary credentials.

questions.question: Users added to an IAM group do not receive the permissions attached to that group.
questions.explanation: Group members inherit the group's permissions.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to configure long-term access for many users?
questions.explanation: Best practice: attach policies to groups, assign users to groups.
options: Attach policies to IAM groups and add users to the groups
Create one IAM user for the whole team
Attach an inline policy to every user

questions.question: Match the photo-app step to the authentication type it needs.
questions.explanation: Four authentication scenarios from the mobile photo app.

pairs.left: Developer builds the app in the AWS account
pairs.right: AWS account authentication

pairs.left: User signs in to the photo app
pairs.right: Application authentication

pairs.left: App uploads the photo to S3
pairs.right: Resource authentication
Database authentication

questions.question: Match the access type to its credentials.
questions.explanation: Console: user name/password. Programmatic: access keys. MFA optional on both.

pairs.right: User name and password
Access key ID and secret access key

questions.question: What does multi-factor authentication (MFA) add?
questions.explanation: MFA prompts users for an authentication code in addition to their password.
options: An extra layer of protection on top of the user name and password

questions.question: Which is a characteristic of an IAM role?
questions.explanation: Roles: temporary credentials, not tied to one person, assumable, used to delegate access.
options: It is assumable by a person, application or service
It is uniquely associated with one person
It can only be used by the root user

questions.question: Which of the following are common use cases for IAM roles? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Roles provide temporary credentials and are used for applications on EC2, cross-account access, mobile apps and federated users. Long-term credentials belong to IAM users.
options: Mobile applications that need to access AWS resources
Cross-account access for an IAM user
An application running on Amazon EC2 that needs to access AWS services
Giving one person permanent long-term credentials

questions.question: A company stores an access key in a text file on a custom AMI so EC2 instances can access DynamoDB. What is the more secure solution?
questions.explanation: Sample exam question: answer D, use an IAM role.
options: Create an IAM role with permissions to the table and launch the instances with the role
Put the access key in an S3 bucket and retrieve it on boot
Pass the access key through instance user data
Get the key from a key server in a private subnet

questions.question: It is acceptable to hard-code AWS credentials in application code if the repository is private.
questions.explanation: Avoid storing credentials in code or public places; use credential files or roles.

questions.question: Match each policy type to the question it answers.
questions.explanation: Identity-based attach to identities; resource-based attach to resources.

pairs.right: What does a particular identity have access to?
Who has access to a particular resource?

questions.question: Account A wants to let Account B access its S3 bucket. Which policy type does Account A use?
questions.explanation: Cross-account resource-based policy; Account B then creates an IAM user policy for its users.
options: An inline policy on Account A's root user
A resource-based (bucket) policy that names Account B
An identity-based policy in Account A

questions.question: Match each policy kind with its characteristic.
questions.explanation: Managed = reusable; inline = embedded 1:1.

pairs.right: Can be attached to multiple users, groups and roles
Strict 1:1 relationship with one entity

questions.question: Which is a benefit of managed policies?
questions.explanation: Managed: reusability, central change management, versioning and rollback, delegation.
options: They are deleted with the user

questions.question: An inline policy can be attached to many users, groups and roles at the same time.
questions.explanation: Inline policies have a strict 1:1 relationship; managed policies are reusable.

questions.question: By default, how does IAM treat a request that no policy mentions?
questions.explanation: All requests are denied by default (implicit deny).
options: It is sent to the root user for approval

questions.question: A group policy allows s3:* but a user policy explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject. What happens when the user tries to delete an object?
questions.explanation: Explicit deny always overrides allow; evaluation order doesn't matter.
options: Denied, because an explicit deny overrides any allow
It depends on the order the policies were created
Allowed, because group policies take precedence
Allowed, because the allow is evaluated first

questions.question: The order in which IAM policies are evaluated affects the final decision.
questions.explanation: Order has no effect; all policies are evaluated.

questions.question: An explicit allow overrides the default deny.
questions.explanation: Default deny < explicit allow < explicit deny.

questions.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
questions.explanation: Start with minimum permissions and grant more as needed.
options: Grant only the minimum permissions needed for the job, then add more as needed
Use the root user only for daily tasks

questions.question: AWS recommends using the account root user credentials for day-to-day tasks.
questions.explanation: Create IAM users and keep root credentials secure.

questions.question: Mateo is in the Admins group but has a user policy that explicitly denies creating IAM groups. What can he do?
questions.explanation: His explicit deny overrides that part of the group allow.
options: Everything Admins can do except creating groups and attaching policies to them

questions.question: Two DBAdmins members temporarily need Amazon RDS access, but the rest of the group doesn't. What should Sofía use?
questions.explanation: Roles are ideal for temporary, delegated access.
options: An IAM role (TempDBRole) with RDS access for those users
Add RDS full access to the DBAdmins group

questions.question: A developer in Account A needs to access resources in Account B. What is the AWS-recommended approach?
questions.explanation: Roles are the standard way to delegate cross-account access with temporary credentials.
options: Assume an IAM role in Account B (cross-account role)
Create a duplicate IAM user in Account B and email the password

questions.question: Order these IAM decisions from weakest to strongest (the last one always wins).
questions.explanation: Everything is denied by default, an explicit allow overrides that, and an explicit deny overrides any allow.
items: Default (implicit) deny
Explicit allow
Explicit deny

questions.question: Drag each credential type to the identity that uses it.
questions.explanation: Users have long-term credentials, roles give temporary ones, groups share permissions.

questions.question: Match each security area to who is responsible for it, the customer or AWS.
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (global infrastructure, hardware, Regions, AZs, edge locations). The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud: data, applications, OS, IAM, network and firewall configuration, encryption.

pairs.right: Customer
Customer
Customer
Customer
Customer
AWS
AWS

questions.question: You are a cloud developer who built an application on AWS. Your manager needs AWS access for a short time to view and test it. What is the right way to give that access?
questions.explanation: Best practice is to give trusted users temporary security credentials through an IAM role instead of sharing long-term credentials.
options: Share your root account user name and password
Hard-code access keys in the application for the manager
Let the manager assume an IAM role that provides temporary security credentials
Share your own IAM user access keys

questions.question: Which of the following are the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Customer = security IN the cloud (data, OS, applications, IAM, firewall and network configuration). AWS = security OF the cloud (facilities, hardware, global infrastructure).
options: Patching the guest operating system on EC2
Maintaining AWS hardware in each Region
Physical security of AWS data centers

questions.question: When an IAM user assumes a role, the user keeps their original permissions in addition to the role's permissions.
questions.explanation: When a user assumes a role, their prior permissions are temporarily forgotten and AWS returns temporary credentials for the role.

questions.question: Drag each security area into the bucket of who is responsible for it.
questions.explanation: The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud, which includes client-side and server-side encryption and networking traffic protection. AWS secures the cloud itself: the host OS/virtualization layer, hardware, and global infrastructure such as Regions, AZs and edge locations.

items.item: Client-side data encryption and data integrity
Hypervisor / virtualization layer that hosts EC2 instances
Compute, storage, database and networking infrastructure

questions.question: Server-side encryption of your file systems and data is AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.
questions.explanation: The shared responsibility slide lists server-side encryption (file system and data) under the customer's responsibility for security in the cloud.

questions.question: Protecting networking traffic (encryption, integrity, identity) is a customer responsibility.
questions.explanation: Networking traffic protection is listed on the customer side, together with network and firewall configuration.

questions.question: What are the objectives of the AWS shared responsibility model? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Because AWS secures the physical infrastructure, the customer's operational burden goes down, while the customer keeps the flexibility and control to build custom applications.
options: Provide needed flexibility and control to the customer
Remove the need for customers to configure IAM
Make AWS responsible for the customer's data
Let AWS patch the guest operating system

questions.question: A company stores data in an S3 bucket and runs a web server on EC2 that uses an RDS database. Who must configure the bucket policies, encryption and S3 Block Public Access on the bucket?
questions.explanation: In the slide example, the customer is responsible for configuring security on the S3 bucket and its objects, using features such as bucket policies, data encryption and S3 Block Public Access.
options: AWS for the bucket, the customer for the objects
Nobody; S3 buckets are secure by default and cannot be changed

questions.question: The exact security responsibilities of a customer depend on which AWS services the customer chooses to use.
questions.explanation: The notes state that the actual customer responsibility details are determined by the AWS services a customer uses and the complexity of their system.

questions.question: An AWS MFA device must be a hardware token; virtual MFA devices are not supported.
questions.explanation: MFA can be hardware-based or a virtual device, such as an app like Google Authenticator running on the user's smartphone.

questions.question: A developer wants to enable MFA for her IAM user but has no hardware token. What can she use?
questions.explanation: The slide says MFA can be hardware-based or a virtual device; the notes give a smartphone app such as Google Authenticator as a virtual MFA device.
options: A virtual MFA device, such as an authenticator app on her smartphone
A second password on the same IAM user
Nothing; MFA requires a hardware device such as a YubiKey
Her access key ID as the second factor

questions.question: Match each MFA factor with its example.
questions.explanation: MFA requires two or more factors: something you know (password), something you have (token/MFA device) and something you are (fingerprint).

pairs.right: A password
A cryptographic token or MFA device
A fingerprint

questions.question: An application needs to call AWS APIs that are protected by MFA. What does it need?
questions.explanation: Enabling MFA for API users requires temporary security credentials; you request them from AWS Security Token Service (STS), passing MFA parameters, and use them to call MFA-protected APIs.
options: MFA-validated temporary security credentials requested from AWS STS
A long-term access key with no MFA
A console user name and password

questions.question: An administrator can attach a policy directly to one IAM user to deny actions that the user's IAM group policy allows.
questions.explanation: When a group's policies are too permissive for one member, an IAM policy attached directly to that user can deny specific actions; the explicit deny overrides the group's allow.

questions.question: Which of the following are features of AWS IAM? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: IAM securely controls individual and group access, integrates with other AWS services, and supports federated identity, granular permissions and MFA.
options: Patches the guest OS of EC2 instances

questions.question: A newly created IAM user can access AWS resources until permissions are explicitly removed.
questions.explanation: Users have no access to AWS resources until permissions are explicitly granted; any action not explicitly allowed is denied.

questions.question: Users authenticated by a corporate identity provider (such as Microsoft Active Directory) need to perform tasks in your AWS account. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: When identities authenticated by a system outside AWS (enterprise or web identity provider) access AWS resources through temporary credentials, this is called identity federation.

questions.question: Why should a mobile app use an IAM role with temporary credentials instead of storing AWS credentials inside the app?
questions.explanation: The notes say you do not want to store AWS credentials with a mobile app, where they are difficult to rotate and users can potentially extract them; roles with temporary credentials are preferred for mobile apps.
options: Roles give the app permanent access that never expires
Mobile apps cannot make AWS API calls with access keys
Roles remove the need for any permissions policy
Stored credentials are hard to rotate and users could extract them

questions.question: You gave an external partner access to your account through an IAM role. The partnership ends. What is the simplest way to remove their access?
questions.explanation: With a role for external access, you don't manage user names and passwords for third parties; if you no longer want them to have access, you modify or delete the role.
options: Disable MFA on your own IAM user

questions.question: You run your IDE remotely on an EC2 instance. How should it get AWS credentials?
questions.explanation: For IDEs on EC2, use AWS managed temporary credentials, which avoids distributing, embedding or storing permanent credentials in the environment.
options: Sign in with the root user
Paste your long-term access keys into the IDE settings
Hard-code the keys in the project source code

questions.question: What are benefits of storing access keys in the AWS credentials file? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: The credentials file keeps keys out of project folders, supports multiple named profiles (e.g. default and prod), and can be reused across projects and SDKs.
options: You can define multiple named sets of credentials (profiles) in one place
You can reuse the same credentials between projects
Credentials are stored outside your projects, so you are unlikely to commit them to version control
Credentials in the file never need rotation

questions.question: Which elements does an IAM policy (a JSON document) define?
questions.explanation: An IAM policy is a JSON document that defines the effect, actions, resources and optional conditions under which an entity can invoke API operations.
options: Region, Availability Zone and instance type
Only the user name and password
Encryption keys and access key IDs
Effect, actions, resources and optional conditions

questions.question: Account A adds a bucket policy that grants Account B access to its S3 bucket. What else is needed for a specific user in Account B to access the bucket?
questions.explanation: The bucket policy names Account B, not individual users; Account B should then create an IAM user policy that allows its user to access Account A's bucket.
options: Account A must share its root credentials with Account B
Account A must create an IAM user for that person
Account B must give that user an IAM policy allowing access to Account A's bucket
Nothing; every user in Account B now has access

questions.question: Match each statement with the policy type it describes.

questions.question: How many RCUs must you provision to read 40 items that are 16 KB in size every second with eventual consistency?
questions.explanation: 16 KB / 4 KB = 4 RCUs per item. 4 × 40 = 160 for strongly consistent reads. Eventually consistent halves it: 160 / 2 = 80 RCUs.

questions.question: How many RCUs must you provision to read 20 items that are 6 KB in size every second with strong consistency?
questions.explanation: Round 6 KB up to 8 KB: 8 / 4 = 2 RCUs per item. 2 × 20 = 40 RCUs (no halving for strong consistency).

questions.question: How many WCUs must you provision to write 10 items that are 2.5 KB in size every second?
questions.explanation: 1 WCU = one 1 KB write per second. Round 2.5 KB up to 3 KB = 3 WCUs per item. 3 × 10 = 30 WCUs.

questions.question: You are developing an application that uses Amazon DynamoDB, and you accidentally deleted some records. Which backup feature lets you restore the table to just before the deletion?
questions.explanation: Point-in-time recovery protects against accidental writes and deletes and can restore the table to any point in the last 35 days. On-demand backups are full backups you create for long-term retention.

questions.question: How many RCUs must you provision to read 15 items that are 9 KB in size every second with strong consistency?

questions.question: An application reads 600 items that are 8 KB in size every minute, using eventually consistent reads. How many RCUs must you provision?
questions.explanation: 600 per minute = 10 per second. 8 KB / 4 KB = 2 RCUs per item, x 10 = 20 for strong consistency; divide by 2 for eventual consistency = 10.

questions.question: An application must read 1,200 items that are 3 KB in size every minute with strong consistency. How many RCUs must you provision?
questions.explanation: 1,200 per minute = 20 per second. 3 KB rounds up to 4 KB = 1 RCU per item, x 20 = 20. Strongly consistent, so no halving.

questions.question: How many RCUs must you provision to read 50 items that are 1 KB in size every second with eventual consistency?

questions.question: How many RCUs must you provision to read 25 items that are 13 KB in size every second with eventual consistency?
questions.explanation: Round 13 KB up to 16 KB, divide by 4 = 4 RCUs per item, x 25 = 100, divide by 2 for eventual consistency = 50.

questions.question: An application reads 30 items that are 12 KB in size every second. Match each read type with the RCUs needed.

questions.question: A table is provisioned with 100 RCUs. How many eventually consistent reads per second of items up to 4 KB can it support?

questions.question: How many WCUs must you provision to write 15 items that are 3.5 KB in size every second?

questions.question: An application writes 300 items that are 1.5 KB in size every minute. How many WCUs must you provision?

questions.question: How many WCUs must you provision to write 40 items that are 0.5 KB in size every second?

questions.question: An application writes 180 items that are 6 KB in size every minute. How many WCUs must you provision?
questions.explanation: 180 per minute = 3 per second. A 6 KB item needs 6 WCUs, x 3 = 18.

questions.explanation: RESTful APIs are stateless and short-lived; WebSocket APIs are stateful and long-lived.

questions.question: Which task can an API gateway proxy handle so the server doesn't have to?
questions.explanation: Proxy tasks: rate limiting, key validation, discarding invalid requests, geo-routing, source filtering.
options: Limit the request rate and validate developer keys

questions.question: What is Amazon API Gateway?
questions.explanation: API Gateway is fully managed and serverless.
options: A fully managed service to create, publish, maintain, monitor and secure APIs at any scale

questions.question: Drag each characteristic to RESTful or WebSocket APIs.
questions.explanation: REST = stateless short-lived; WebSocket = stateful bidirectional.

items.item: Uses HTTP methods like GET and POST
More efficient for chatty, real-time applications

questions.question: A real-time chat application needs bidirectional communication. Which API type should you create?
questions.explanation: WebSockets provide real-time, two-way communication.

questions.question: Match each API type with its description.
questions.explanation: REST API vs HTTP API.

pairs.right: Full control over requests and responses, more features
Only proxy functionality, lowest cost and latency

questions.question: You need a simple API that proxies requests to Lambda at the lowest cost and latency. Which type?
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs are designed for lowest cost and latency.

questions.question: Match each endpoint type with its description.
questions.explanation: Edge-optimized and private are REST only.

pairs.right: Uses a managed CloudFront distribution for global clients
For clients in the same AWS Region
Accessible only from within your VPC

questions.question: Which endpoint type is supported by REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs?
questions.explanation: All API types support Regional endpoints.

questions.question: Your API clients are distributed globally and you want built-in DDoS protection without managing CloudFront. Which endpoint?
questions.explanation: Edge-optimized uses an API Gateway-managed CloudFront distribution.

questions.question: Private endpoints are available for HTTP APIs.
questions.explanation: Edge-optimized and private endpoints are REST only.

questions.question: A mock integration returns default data without calling a backend, which is useful for prototyping front ends.
questions.explanation: The lab used mock endpoints before connecting Lambda.

questions.question: Match each Lambda integration type with its behavior.
questions.explanation: Proxy = pass-through; non-proxy = wrapped and mappable.

pairs.right: Response passed through; Lambda must format it
API Gateway wraps the response and can transform it with VTL

questions.question: In which language are API Gateway mapping templates written?
questions.explanation: Mapping templates use Apache VTL.

questions.question: In a Lambda proxy integration, API Gateway transforms the response with VTL mapping templates.
questions.explanation: Mapping templates are used in non-proxy integrations; proxy integrations pass the response through.

questions.question: Match each integration type to its use.
questions.explanation: Integration options.

pairs.right: Route directly to an AWS service API like SQS-SendMessage
Forward a route to an internet HTTP endpoint, e.g. a monolith
Reach VPC resources through a VPC link and load balancer
Return fixed data with no backend

questions.question: You are migrating a monolith on EC2 to Lambda one route at a time. Which integration helps most?
questions.explanation: Map all routes to the monolith with HTTP proxy, then remap routes to Lambda one by one.

questions.question: What connects API Gateway to private resources (EC2, ECS, EKS) inside a VPC?
questions.explanation: Private integrations use a VPC link (ALB/NLB).
options: A VPC link with a load balancer

questions.question: What is an API Gateway stage?
questions.explanation: Stages are snapshots, identified by API ID + stage name, included in the URL.
options: A named snapshot of an API deployment that is part of the invoke URL

questions.question: A stage name is not part of the URL used to invoke the API.
questions.explanation: Stages are included in the invoke URL, e.g. .../dev/products and .../prod/products.

questions.question: A developer needs dev and prod environments; the backend Lambda function has dev and prod aliases. What requires the LEAST configuration?
questions.explanation: Sample exam question: answer B.
options: One API on prod with a canary for dev
Two separate REST APIs, one per alias
One REST API using a stage variable for the alias, deployed to dev and prod stages
One API on dev with a canary for prod

questions.question: Stage variables let each stage point to a different backend, such as a different Lambda alias.
questions.explanation: e.g. lambdaAlias = dev / beta / prod.

questions.question: What is a canary deployment in API Gateway?
questions.explanation: Canary: split traffic between production and canary releases.
options: Sending a percentage of a stage's traffic to a new version for testing

questions.question: Which of the following API Gateway features protect your API from unwanted traffic? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: API Gateway protections include resource policies, AWS WAF (SQL injection, XSS), throttling and usage plans. Streams and X-Ray do not block traffic.

questions.question: You want to limit access to a REST API's dev stage to your office IP range without using WAF. What do you use?
questions.explanation: REST API resource policies can restrict by source IP or account.

questions.question: Which service protects APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS)?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF protects against common web exploits.

questions.question: Which request is NOT cross-origin relative to https://example.com?
questions.explanation: Cross-origin = different domain, subdomain, port or protocol.

questions.question: Before a non-simple cross-origin request, what does the browser send?
questions.explanation: The browser sends an OPTIONS preflight.

questions.question: CORS is enforced by the browser, so it matters only when your clients are browsers.
questions.explanation: CORS is a browser security feature.

questions.question: What is the default Region-wide throttling quota shared by all APIs in an account?
questions.explanation: 10,000 rps, a soft limit.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code means a request was throttled by API Gateway?
questions.explanation: 429 indicates throttling.

questions.question: How do you throttle individual API clients (such as partners) on a REST API?
questions.explanation: Usage plans throttle by client (and client + method).

questions.question: Stage or method throttling rates can be set higher than the account-level rate.
questions.explanation: They cannot be higher than the account-level rate.

questions.question: Match each authorization option with how it works.
questions.explanation: Four authorization options.

pairs.right: Leaves access open
Uses IAM and AWS credentials (signed requests)
Amazon Cognito user pools or another JWT provider
Function validates a bearer token or request parameters

questions.question: Match each CloudWatch metric to what it measures.
questions.explanation: Default API Gateway metrics.

pairs.right: Time from when API Gateway receives a request to when it responds
Backend request/response time
Number of API calls in a period
Client-side and server-side errors

questions.question: Match each monitoring tool with its purpose.
questions.explanation: Monitoring tools.

pairs.right: Trace and analyze requests end to end
Assess, audit and evaluate configuration changes
Record actions taken by users, roles or services on API Gateway
Log who accessed the API and how, per stage

questions.question: The IntegrationLatency metric measures the full round trip from client request to API Gateway response.
questions.explanation: That is Latency. IntegrationLatency measures the backend request/response time.

questions.question: API Gateway caching reduces calls to your backend and improves latency, and can be set up per stage or method.
questions.explanation: Caching benefits.

questions.question: Clients of an API are receiving HTTP 429 errors. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: 429 Too Many Requests = throttling.
options: The Lambda function has a syntax error

questions.question: A website hosted on an S3 domain calls an API Gateway API with JavaScript, and the browser blocks the request. What should the developer do?
questions.explanation: Cross-origin browser requests need CORS support on the API.

questions.question: A GET endpoint returns the same product list for every user and the backend is overloaded. Which API Gateway feature reduces backend calls?
questions.explanation: Caching serves repeated requests from the cache (CacheHitCount).

questions.question: Put the API Gateway request flow in order.
questions.explanation: Client → method request → integration request → backend → integration response → method response.
items: Method request
Integration request
Backend
Integration response
Method response

questions.question: Order the throttling levels in the order API Gateway applies them (first applied at the top).
questions.explanation: Throttling is applied from the most granular to the least granular.
items: Per client and method (usage plan)
Per client (usage plan)
Per method or route
Per stage
Account level (10,000 rps)

questions.question: Drag each feature to where it is available.
questions.explanation: Edge-optimized and private endpoints, caching, usage plans, resource policies and client SDKs are REST-only. Regional endpoints work for all.

questions.question: A developer is building an API using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The API needs to transform incoming JSON requests before passing them to the Lambda function. Where should this transformation be configured?
questions.explanation: With a non-proxy (custom) integration, API Gateway mapping templates written in VTL can modify requests and responses: add, delete or edit parameters.

questions.question: When a RESTful API is called, the server transfers to the client a representation of the state of the requested resource.
questions.explanation: That is what Representational State Transfer (REST) means: the client receives a representation of the resource's state.

questions.question: API mock endpoints are only useful for abstracting real endpoints.
questions.explanation: Mocks can abstract options, but they are also useful for prototyping and testing front ends before the backend exists, and API Gateway uses a mock endpoint for the CORS OPTIONS method.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid uses of an API Gateway mock endpoint? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: A mock endpoint returns default data without a backend. It is used for front-end prototyping and testing, and API Gateway uses one for the CORS OPTIONS method.
options: Permanently storing data like a database
Returning default data without calling a backend
Prototyping and testing a front end before the backend is ready
Handling the OPTIONS method when CORS is configured on a REST API

questions.question: Match each HTTP response status code range with its meaning.
questions.explanation: Slide 10: 20x codes are successes, 40x codes tell the client it must change something (e.g. wrong password), and 50x codes signal a server-side problem such as a programming error or resource failure.

pairs.right: Successful response
The client must do something differently
Something went wrong that was not the client's fault

extra: The request was redirected to CloudFront

questions.question: Which URL prefix does a WebSocket connection use instead of http://?
questions.explanation: Slide 10: WebSockets use a different, bidirectional protocol with URLs that start with ws:// (or wss:// for the secure variant).

questions.question: Following best practice, which protocols should a client use to call an API over HTTP and over WebSockets?
questions.explanation: Slide 10: with any protocol it is a best practice to use the secure variants, such as HTTPS and WSS (Secure WebSockets).

questions.question: SOAP is an XML-based protocol, and even SOAP clients usually transmit their requests over HTTP.
questions.explanation: Slide 10: API requests can use SOAP (an XML-based protocol), WebSockets or HTTP; a client using SOAP still usually transmits requests by using HTTP.

questions.question: An API that uses HTTP but does not follow REST principles is not a valid API.
questions.explanation: Slide 11: REST is only an architectural style; non-RESTful APIs that use HTTP are valid and quite common.

questions.question: Which of the following tasks can an API gateway (proxy) take over from your servers? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 14: an API gateway proxy can rate-limit, validate developer keys and drop invalid requests, and limit or reroute requests by language headers or geographical region, so fewer requests reach the server.
options: Compile and deploy the server code
Discard invalid requests before they reach the server
Run database queries for the backend
Route geo-specific requests to the correct server

questions.question: How are you charged for Amazon API Gateway?
questions.explanation: Slide 15: API Gateway is fully managed and serverless; you pay only for the API calls that you receive and the amount of data transferred out.
options: Only for the API calls received and the amount of data transferred out
Per developer account that creates APIs
Per provisioned server instance behind the API
A fixed hourly price per API, whether used or not

questions.question: Putting Amazon API Gateway in front of DynamoDB, instead of letting client applications connect to the table directly, gives you more control and flexibility.
questions.explanation: Slide 15: you might use API Gateway instead of having clients connect directly to DynamoDB, which gives you more control and flexibility; API Gateway acts as the front door to backend services.

questions.question: Why can't a client application call a Lambda function directly with a standard HTTP request?
questions.explanation: Slide 18: Lambda endpoints are not publicly accessible URIs, so you must either use an AWS SDK or put something like an API Gateway HTTP API in front of the function.
options: Lambda functions only respond to WebSocket connections
Lambda requires a Regional endpoint in the client's VPC
Lambda endpoints are not publicly accessible URIs

questions.question: Compared with a standard REST API, up to how much can you save by using an HTTP API in API Gateway?
questions.explanation: Slide 18: HTTP APIs are lightweight, have lower latency and cost less; savings can be up to 70% compared with the standard REST API.

questions.question: A team is choosing between a REST API and an HTTP API. Which requirements point to a REST API? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 18: REST APIs are 'advanced mode' with request/response manipulation, customized authentication and mock endpoints; unless you need advanced features or need to monetize the API, choose HTTP.
options: Only a simple proxy in front of a Lambda function at the lowest cost
Fine-grained control over highly customized authentication

questions.question: Why are WebSockets more efficient than HTTP for a chatty application that sends many small messages?
questions.explanation: Slide 21: every HTTP request carries 'envelope bloat' (headers, bearer tokens); a WebSocket two-way pipe sends just the data once the connection is set up.
options: WebSockets send messages only over a VPC link
WebSockets compress every message with gzip automatically
After the connection is established, messages are sent without repeating the HTTP envelope (headers, tokens) each time
WebSockets cache responses at edge locations

questions.question: With WebSockets, each message still carries the full HTTP headers and authentication token, just like a separate HTTP request.
questions.explanation: Slide 21: after the initial setup, both sides send small efficient messages through the two-way pipe without additional per-message information.

questions.question: WebSocket routing in API Gateway can choose which backend service to invoke based on characteristics such as the message content.
questions.explanation: Slide 21: you can set WebSocket routing to invoke backends such as Lambda, Kinesis or an HTTP endpoint based on characteristics like message content.

questions.question: Drag each tool to how it is used with API Gateway in the slides: developing APIs or deploying them as infrastructure as code.
questions.explanation: Slide 22: you develop APIs with the console, AWS CLI or OpenAPI (Swagger) definitions, and deploy them with frameworks such as AWS SAM, CloudFormation and the AWS CDK.

questions.question: Which statement about AWS SAM is correct?
questions.explanation: Slide 22: AWS SAM (and the SAM CLI) is useful for locally testing and deploying serverless APIs; it is a superset of CloudFormation with simplified syntax.
options: It is a superset of CloudFormation with simplified syntax for serverless components
It generates client SDKs for REST APIs
It is a web firewall that protects APIs
It replaces CloudFormation and does not use templates

questions.question: An API with ID a1b2c3 is deployed to the prod stage in us-east-2. Which URL does the client use to invoke it?
questions.explanation: Slide 25: the base URL is https://{restapi_id}.execute-api.{region}.amazonaws.com/{stage_name}/.

questions.question: According to the slides, which are ways to create an API in API Gateway? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 33: you can create APIs by using the AWS CLI, the API Gateway console, or by importing an OpenAPI definition.

questions.question: You can build an API in API Gateway from an imported OpenAPI or Swagger definition file.
questions.explanation: Slide 32: OpenAPI (formerly Swagger) is a declarative definition file; you can import it to build an API and export an API's definition to document it.

questions.question: When you create an HTTP API integrated with a Lambda function, you must create a stage and deploy to it manually before it can be called.
questions.explanation: Slides 26 and 55: an HTTP API gets a default stage that automatically deploys changes; a REST API is the one where you must create at least one stage and deploy to it.

questions.question: An API needs to read products and update products. What is the best practice for structuring it?
questions.explanation: Slides 27 and 33: as a best practice, use different paths to perform different actions and connect them to different backend integrations (e.g. GET routes to readFn, PUT to updateFn).
options: Create a separate API for every HTTP method
Send every action to one default endpoint and parse it in a single function
Use a mock integration for writes and a proxy for reads
Use different paths and methods for different actions, each connected to the appropriate backend integration

questions.question: What does the greedy path variable {proxy+} do on a route such as /products/{proxy+}?
questions.explanation: Slide 30: {proxy+} lets one integration absorb any nested paths; it is simpler to build, but using more specific paths is generally the better practice.
options: Sends any nested path under /products to a single integration
Creates a separate Lambda function for each nested path

questions.question: Match each WebSocket API route key with when API Gateway calls it.
questions.explanation: Slide 31: besides custom routes chosen by the required route selection expression, WebSocket APIs use $connect, $disconnect and $default.

pairs.right: A persistent connection between the client and the API is being initiated
The client or the server disconnects from the API
The route selection expression cannot be evaluated or no route matches

extra: A message is throttled with a 429 error

questions.question: For Regional endpoints accessed by websites, it is a best practice to put a CloudFront distribution in front of them.
questions.explanation: Slide 35: setting up CloudFront in front of Regional endpoints helps protect against DDoS attacks and reduces round-trip time.

questions.question: API Gateway can generate client SDKs for REST APIs, HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs.
questions.explanation: Slide 36: client SDKs (Android, iOS, JavaScript, Ruby, Java) are generated only for REST APIs in API Gateway.

questions.question: Why do the slides recommend calling an API Gateway endpoint with HTTPS requests rather than a generated client SDK?
questions.explanation: Slide 36: building the signed payload with the SDK is non-trivial and puts API credentials on the client, a bad security practice; plain HTTPS requests are simpler and more secure.
options: HTTPS requests are cached automatically at the edge
Generated SDKs are only available for HTTP APIs
The SDK approach forces you to handle API credentials on the client side and is harder to code
Generated SDKs cannot be used from JavaScript

questions.question: Which backends can API Gateway integrate with? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 37: API Gateway can run Lambda functions, connect to DynamoDB or S3, start Step Functions, call HTTP endpoints on Elastic Beanstalk or EC2, call public internet endpoints, and integrate directly with services like Kinesis.
options: HTTP endpoints on the public internet that are not hosted on AWS
Only AWS services in the same Availability Zone
Only EC2 instances with public IP addresses

questions.question: VPC links that reach resources in a VPC through an Elastic Load Balancer are available with both REST and HTTP APIs.
questions.explanation: Slide 37: with both REST and HTTP APIs, you can connect to a VPC link that allows access to resources in a VPC through an Elastic Load Balancer.

questions.question: A Lambda function behind a proxy integration must tell the client that it lacks permission. How should it return the error?
questions.explanation: Slide 41: with a Lambda proxy integration, the function uses the output format API Gateway requires and includes the error (e.g. statusCode 403) in its customized response; with non-proxy you map errors to HTTP error responses.
options: Configure a VTL mapping template on the integration response
Include a statusCode such as 403 and the message in its own formatted response
Return plain JSON and let API Gateway convert it to 403
Throw an exception so API Gateway returns 200 OK

questions.question: In a non-proxy integration, if function errors are not mapped to standard HTTP error responses, the client can receive them with a 200 status.
questions.explanation: Slides 39 and 41: in a non-proxy integration API Gateway wraps a successful call with status 200; map function errors to HTTP error responses so clients don't receive them as 200.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of first-class integrations for HTTP APIs? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 45: a first-class integration connects an HTTP API route directly to an AWS service API, for example SQS-SendMessage or StepFunctions-StartExecution.
options: HTTP proxy to an EC2 monolith

questions.question: With a first-class integration, API Gateway automatically knows how to map the request to the target service, so you do not need to provide any parameter mapping.
questions.explanation: Slides 45-46: each service needs a different mapping, so you must map values from the request's body, query string or headers to the object the target AWS service requires.

questions.question: A private integration uses a VPC link. What can the VPC link connect API Gateway to? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 48: API Gateway accesses resources in a VPC through a VPC link with an Application Load Balancer, a Network Load Balancer, or resources registered in AWS Cloud Map.
options: Resources registered with an AWS Cloud Map service

questions.question: What do you use to modify requests and responses for HTTP APIs?
questions.explanation: Slide 51: HTTP APIs use parameter mapping, where you specify the request or response parameters to modify and how; VTL mapping templates are used with REST non-proxy integrations.

questions.question: Parameter mapping can modify any header, including reserved headers.
questions.explanation: Slide 51: you cannot configure request or response mappings for reserved headers; you can append, overwrite or remove other headers and query strings and override paths.

questions.question: A stage must be selected when deploying a REST API or a WebSocket API.
questions.explanation: Slide 55: to deploy you create a deployment and associate it with a stage; REST and WebSocket APIs require a stage, while HTTP APIs deploy to a default stage.

questions.question: A developer wants the dev stage to use a development database and the prod stage to use the production database without writing different code. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Slide 57: stage variables are set per stage and let you target different resources, such as a development database or a Lambda alias, without writing different code.

questions.question: Put the steps of a canary release on a stage in order.
questions.explanation: Slides 58-59: canary settings split traffic at random with a preconfigured ratio; if results are good you increase the percentage, and promoting the canary fully deploys the stage.
items: Add canary settings to the stage of a regular deployment
Send a small percentage of the stage traffic to the canary
Monitor results and increase the canary percentage
Promote the canary so the stage is fully deployed to production

questions.question: In a canary release, the base version and the canary version run on two different stages.
questions.explanation: Slide 58: the base version remains deployed as the production release on the same stage; traffic on that stage is split at random between production and canary.

questions.question: HTTP APIs can use IAM resource policies to restrict access to an API by IP address.
questions.explanation: Slide 63: resource policies are for REST APIs; HTTP APIs currently cannot use resource policies this way.

questions.question: You want users in a different AWS account to call your REST API. Which feature lets you allow this?
questions.explanation: Slide 63: with REST APIs you can use IAM resource policies to control access, for example allowing users in a different AWS account or limiting a stage to an office IP range.
options: An IAM resource policy on the API

questions.question: Which statements describe custom domains for API Gateway? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 64: custom domains use ACM-managed SSL certificates, support wildcard domains, and support multiple domains through base path mapping.
options: Custom domains are only available for WebSocket APIs
Multiple domains are supported through base path mapping
SSL certificates are managed through AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)

questions.question: An API Gateway client certificate lets EC2 backends confirm requests come from API Gateway. How long is it valid?
questions.explanation: Slide 65: API Gateway generates a client-side SSL certificate; the backend verifies requests with the public key, and the certificate expires after 365 days.

questions.question: Mutual TLS between API Gateway and IoT devices is possible only when you use a custom domain for the API.
questions.explanation: Slide 65: mutual TLS, where both API Gateway and the device have certificates, is possible only with a custom domain so the API has a certificate the device can confirm.

questions.question: On what basis can AWS WAF block requests to an API? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 66: AWS WAF can block by IP ranges, country or region, and user agents, bots and scrapers; it also matches string or regex patterns and protects against SQL injection and XSS.
options: Specific user agents, bad bots and content scrapers

questions.question: Simple read-only AJAX GET requests always require a CORS preflight request.
questions.explanation: Slide 68: simple AJAX requests such as GETs are read-only and are considered simple requests that do not require CORS support; non-simple requests need a preflight.

questions.question: CORS can be enabled only on REST APIs, not on HTTP APIs.
questions.explanation: Slide 69: you can enable and configure CORS on both REST and HTTP APIs; for REST, API Gateway sets up a mock endpoint to handle OPTIONS, and setup is simpler for HTTP APIs.

questions.question: When you enable CORS on an API, what do you specify for API Gateway to use in its response to the preflight request?
questions.explanation: Slide 68: you specify the allowed headers, methods and origins; requests that do not meet these criteria generate an error.
options: The cache TTL and encryption key
The usage plan and API keys

questions.question: The 10,000 requests per second account-level throttling quota is a hard limit that cannot be raised.
questions.explanation: Slide 70: all APIs in an account share a Region-wide quota of 10,000 rps, which is a soft limit that can be raised on request.

questions.question: Besides throttling, what else can a usage plan control for a client's API key?
questions.explanation: Slide 72: a usage plan sets throttling limits on request rate and a quota on how many requests an API key can use in a specific time frame; API keys are unique string values for REST APIs.
options: A quota on how many requests the key can make in a time period
The Region the API is deployed in

questions.question: A developer wants users to sign in through Amazon Cognito user pools and have API Gateway validate their tokens. Which authorizer type is this?
questions.explanation: Slide 76: JWT-based authorization includes Amazon Cognito user pools (REST APIs) or other JWT providers (HTTP APIs); Cognito is a simple identity provider for JWT authorizers.

questions.question: An API uses IAM authorization. What happens to a request that is not signed?
questions.explanation: Slide 76: with IAM authorization the client uses IAM credentials (usually temporary, via the SDK); requests that are not signed return a permissions error.
options: It is passed to a Lambda authorizer
It is redirected to Amazon Cognito
It is answered from the cache

questions.question: What is an advantage of a Lambda authorizer that passes an isAuthorized value to the target function?
questions.explanation: Slide 78: the authorizer validates custom criteria and passes isAuthorized to the end target, which can handle a rejection more gracefully than an abrupt 40X from API Gateway.
options: It removes the need for any authentication
It caches every response for one hour
The target function can handle a rejection gracefully instead of the client getting an abrupt 40X error

questions.question: You can configure a different authorizer for each route of an API, or share one authorizer across multiple routes.
questions.explanation: Slide 76: you can configure distinct authorizers for each route of an API, or use the same authorizer for multiple routes.

questions.question: How long does CloudWatch keep API Gateway metric statistics?
questions.explanation: Slide 81: API Gateway sends metrics to CloudWatch every minute by default, and the statistics are recorded for 15 months so you can view historical performance.

questions.question: To use access logging, you must first create the CloudWatch log group and then point the stage to it.
questions.explanation: Slide 82: API Gateway creates the log groups for error logs, but for access logs you create the log group and then enable access logging on the stage pointing to it.

questions.question: Match each question with the tool that answers it.
questions.explanation: Slides 81 and 83: CloudTrail records who changed what and when, X-Ray traces requests end to end, AWS Config checks compliance of configurations, and CloudWatch collects metrics such as 5XXError.

pairs.left: Who modified the API's resources and when?
pairs.right: AWS CloudTrail

pairs.left: Where are problems occurring across my distributed application?
pairs.right: AWS X-Ray

pairs.left: Does this modification comply with our rules?
pairs.right: AWS Config

pairs.left: How many 5XX errors did the API return in the last hour?
pairs.right: Amazon CloudWatch

questions.question: Caching is enabled on a REST API stage. Which metric counts requests that were served from the API cache rather than the backend?
questions.explanation: Slide 85: CacheHitCount counts requests served from the API cache; CacheMissCount counts requests served from the backend when caching is enabled.

questions.question: CacheMissCount is the number of requests served from the backend in a given period when caching is enabled.
questions.explanation: Slide 85: CacheMissCount counts requests served from the backend while caching is enabled; CacheHitCount counts those served from the cache.

questions.question: API Gateway caching is charged only for the hours in which the cache actually serves requests.
questions.explanation: Slide 85: caching is priced hourly whether the cache is used or not.

questions.question: Which statements about API Gateway caching are correct? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 85: for REST APIs the cache has a configurable TTL, optional encryption, and cache keys based on path, headers and query strings.
options: You can encrypt the data stored in the cache
Caching is available for HTTP APIs only
Cache keys can use the path, headers and query strings
Cached values have a TTL that you can modify

questions.question: Compressing very small payloads might increase their final size and add latency, so you should test to find an optimal compression size.
questions.explanation: Slide 86: compressing small data can increase its size, and compression/decompression can add latency and compute time, so run tests to find an optimal value.

questions.question: Which content codings does API Gateway support for payload compression? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 86: the supported content codings are deflate, gzip and identity; clients send compressed payloads with an appropriate Content-Encoding header.

questions.question: Match each deployment model with its characteristic.
questions.explanation: Levels of abstraction.

pairs.right: Heavy capital expense and guessed capacity
Hardware independence and faster provisioning
Platform independence and isolation/sandboxing
No OS instances to manage and pay per usage

questions.question: Which is a characteristic of serverless computing?
questions.explanation: Serverless: no OS, flexible scaling, pay per usage, fault tolerance, zero maintenance.
options: No OS instances to manage and built-in fault tolerance
Guessed capacity and years of maintenance
You must patch the operating system

questions.question: What is AWS Lambda?
questions.explanation: Lambda runs code in response to events and scales automatically.
options: A serverless compute service that runs code without provisioning or managing servers

Put all business logic inside the handler
Store state in memory between invocations

An S3 bucket named after the function

Non-indexed key-value data not used for searching

Embed credentials in the function code
Store AWS access keys in environment variables

questions.question: You are deploying a Lambda function using the container image option. Which of the following are the correct steps?
questions.explanation: Container image: choose a runtime and Linux distribution when creating the image, package code and dependencies as an image, and upload it to Amazon ECR. The "compress and upload" steps are the .zip option.

Choose a runtime and Linux distribution, package your code and dependencies as a container image, then upload the image to the container registry (Amazon ECR)
Package your code and dependencies as a container image, then upload the image to an S3 bucket

questions.question: Put the steps for deploying a Lambda function as a container image in order.

Package your code and dependencies as a container image
Upload the image to your container registry (Amazon ECR)

questions.question: With the Lambda polling (pull) model, what happens if, after Lambda polls the queue for a record, the invocation fails or times out?
questions.explanation: For queue sources such as SQS, a failed message returns to the queue and is retried until it succeeds or the retry limit or retention period is reached. Failed messages can go to an OnFailure destination or a dead-letter queue.
options: The failed message returns to the queue and Lambda retries it; if it keeps failing, it can be sent to a dead-letter queue
The function ignores the failed message

questions.question: One of the use cases of the Lambda polling (pull) model is a chatbot.
questions.explanation: Polling is for streams and queues (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams). Chatbots built with Amazon Lex invoke Lambda directly (push model).

questions.question: Which of the following event sources use the Lambda polling (event source mapping) model? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Lambda polls queues and streams: SQS, Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams. S3 invokes asynchronously and API Gateway invokes synchronously.

questions.question: With asynchronous invocation, if an error occurs Lambda retries the invocation twice and can send failed events to a dead-letter queue.
questions.explanation: Async: Lambda queues the event, retries twice on error, and can send failures to a configured dead-letter queue.

questions.question: Lambda charges you every time it polls an event source, even when no records are found.
questions.explanation: Polling does not incur any charge. You are charged only if actions result from a poll.

questions.question: As you move from on premises to virtual servers, containers and then serverless, the level of abstraction increases. What is the main benefit of this for developers?
questions.explanation: Abstracting the infrastructure layer removes operational tasks, so you can focus more on business logic (slide 8).
options: They can run code only on dedicated hardware
They must provision capacity further in advance
They gain more control over the operating system
They can focus more on the business logic of their applications

questions.question: With serverless computing, you don't pay for any infrastructure when your code isn't running.
questions.explanation: Slide 8 notes: you don't pay for infrastructure when the code isn't running, and code runs only when needed.

questions.question: Drag each task to show whether you still do it with serverless, or only when you manage servers.

questions.question: Match each principle of building modern serverless applications with its benefit.

Choose features and capacity that suit each service's data
Faster delivery and less effort integrating services
Replicate environments and deploy more often with confidence

questions.question: Match each application style with its description.

pairs.right: Does everything; one artifact to deploy
Does one thing; deployed independently

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of microservices compared to a monolithic application? Select more than one answer.
questions.explanation: Slide 10 notes: microservices let you scale, choose stacks/data stores, and deploy each service independently; however, the effort to get started is higher.
options: A single shared database for all features
Deploy changes independently as often as desired
Lower initial effort to get started
Choose the best technology stack and data store for each service

questions.question: Moving to a microservices-based serverless application requires less initial effort than building a monolith.
questions.explanation: Slide 10 notes: with a modern serverless application the effort to get started is higher; agility increases after the initial learning curve.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of AWS Lambda? Select more than one answer.
